rationale: Electrophysiological assessment shows that an electronegative dark-adapted full-field ERG is a key diagnostic clue separating CLN3-associated disease from early-onset Stargardt disease (STGD1), where dark-adapted ERGs are typically preserved or only mildly reduced. However, its classification as a 'highly sensitive' discriminator at presentation is contradicted by cohort studies showing that a significant fraction of CLN3 patients present with completely extinguished or undetectable ERG waveforms rather than an electronegative configuration. For example, Wright et al. (2020) observed electronegative ERGs in only 4 of 8 patients (50%), whereas the remaining 4 (50%) exhibited undetectable ERGs due to severe concurrent a-wave loss, and Kuper et al. (2021) similarly noted that dark-adapted responses in CLN3 were either absent or electronegative.

evidence.text: In a comparative retrospective cohort, dark-adapted full-field ERGs were either absent or electronegative in CLN3 patients (n=18), whereas in early-onset STGD1 patients (n=20), dark-adapted responses were unaffected (8/11) or mildly reduced (3/11), and 0/20 showed an electronegative ERG.

evidence.text: Review of negative ERGs in genetic retinal disorders highlights that while electronegative waveforms occur in CLN3 due to inner retinal dysfunction (selective b-wave reduction), variants in CLN3 can also give rise to nonsyndromic retinal dystrophy, and ERGs rapidly progress toward extinction.

conflicts: High sensitivity claimed for electronegative ERG alone (100% in Sakti et al., 5/5) is directly contradicted by Wright et al., where only 50% (4/8) exhibited an electronegative ERG and 50% (4/8) had completely undetectable ERGs.

Kuper et al. demonstrated that dark-adapted full-field ERGs are either electronegative OR absent/undetectable in CLN3 disease; thus, relying strictly on the presence of an electronegative waveform misses cases that present with severe global retinal dysfunction.

new_directions.question_text: What is the combined sensitivity and specificity of paired electrophysiology (electronegative or unrecordable ERG) and peripheral blood smear testing (vacuolated lymphocytes) for differentiating CLN3 from STGD1 and CRB1/RPGR rod-cone dystrophies?
new_directions.rationale: Because 50% of CLN3 patients have undetectable rather than electronegative ERGs at clinical diagnosis, testing whether peripheral vacuolated lymphocyte screening recovers 100% sensitivity will resolve diagnostic delays.

new_directions.question_text: At what disease duration or visual acuity threshold does the CLN3 dark-adapted ERG transition from an electronegative configuration to completely extinguished?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the temporal window during which an electronegative ERG can be captured will define the exact clinical stage where this biomarker is informative versus when photoreceptor death causes signal ablation.
